newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: OTC fever boosts volumes in Singapore stock market.
newsitem.headline: OTC fever boosts volumes in Singapore stock market.

text.p: Frenzied buying of Malaysian stocks traded over the counter (OTC) on Wednesday boosted volumes on the Stock Exchange of Singapore, dealers said.
"The volumes are mainly generated by Malaysian shares. A lot of these shares are cross-listed and enjoy a spill over effect from the firmer Kuala Lumpur stock market," said a dealer.

Turnover was a hectic 530 million shares, with Malaysian shares accounting for about 60 percent. Today's volume on the local bourse is one of the highest in recent years, said an exchange official. Gainers outpaced losers by 373 to 87.
Malaysia's Sri Hartamas, MBf Holdings, Insas Bhd and Berjaya Industrial raked up a combined volume of over 87 million shares.
Besides speculative issues, funds were also seen buying Singapore banking stocks and selected blue chips.
The Straits Times Industrials Index climbed 27.59 points to end at 2,224.64 while the UOB OTC index closed off its new high of 1,324.09 at 1,322.50, up 19.81 points.

Leading gainers were foreign tranches of OCBC, Singapore Press, UOB and DBS, rising between S$0.50-S$1.00 (US$0.35-$0.71) each. Funds buying of Lung Kee Metal pushed it to a new year high of US$0.91 before it ended at US$0.905, up US$0.06. Hong Leong Prop warrants jumped 27.19 percent to S$1.45.
